unit.title: Establish and maintain community, government and business partnerships

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A municipal corporation wants to reduce youth unemployment in Spanish Town. Why might it build partnerships with community groups, government agencies and local businesses together?
options: Each sector holds resources and reach the others lack
It lets the corporation pass its duties to the businesses
It means the corporation no longer needs a budget
Businesses are required by law to fund council projects

questions.stem: Before approaching a chamber of commerce about a town-centre clean-up, what should a public officer find out first?
options: How much the chamber's officers are paid each year
Which political party the chamber's president supports
What the members want to gain and can contribute
How quickly the chamber can sign a funding cheque

questions.stem: An agency is starting work in a rural community in Clarendon where it has no contacts. What is the best first step?
options: Hold a press launch in Kingston announcing the project
Meet recognised local leaders and groups to listen first
Send letters telling residents what the agency will do
Hire a firm from outside the parish to run the project

questions.stem: What is 'asset mapping' in community partnership work?
options: Listing the agency's vehicles and buildings for insurance
Drawing a map of land owned by private businesses
Valuing the community's property for tax purposes
Finding the skills, groups and resources a community has

questions.stem: A Member of Parliament asks to launch an agency's community partnership at a party rally. How should the agency respond?
options: Agree, since the MP represents the area
Agree, as long as the rally is held on a weekend
Offer a non-party official event instead
Ask the MP to pay for the launch event instead

questions.stem: Three government agencies each run separate youth programmes in the same Montego Bay community, and residents are confused. What should the agencies do?
options: Agree shared aims, divide roles and coordinate their work
Compete to see which agency's programme attracts the most youths
Keep working separately and leave residents to choose
Close all three programmes and start again next year

questions.stem: In meetings between a large ministry, a big hotel chain and a small fishing cooperative, the cooperative's members rarely speak. What should the convenor do?
options: Move on, since silence means they agree with the plan
Ask the hotel chain to speak for the fishers as well
Hold every meeting in the ministry's boardroom in Kingston
Use smaller sessions and meet the fishers where they work

questions.stem: Which argument is most likely to persuade a local hardware firm to join a community housing repair partnership?
options: It must join because the agency is a public body
It gains goodwill, local trust and a stronger market
It will receive the agency's contracts without bidding
It will be excused from paying its business taxes

questions.stem: A business offers to sponsor an agency's community event if its logo appears on the agency's licence application forms. What should the officer do?
options: Accept, since the sponsorship saves public money
Decline, as it could suggest favour in licensing
Accept but tell no one about the arrangement
Put the logo on half of the forms as a compromise

questions.stem: An agency's partnership with a community development committee has gone quiet since the project launch a year ago. What is the best way to maintain the relationship?
options: Wait until the next project needs the committee's help
Send a single letter thanking them for their past help
Contact them only if a complaint is made about the project
Keep regular contact, share progress and seek their views

questions.stem: The officer who built an agency's partnerships with local businesses is being transferred. What should the manager do?
options: Arrange handover meetings and update the contact records
Let the businesses find out when their calls go unanswered
Ask the officer to keep the contacts as personal ones
Start every relationship again from the very beginning

questions.stem: Why should an agency keep a register of its community, government and business partners?
options: To list the partners who should be avoided in the future
To record which partners are friends of the manager
To track contacts, interests, commitments and history
To share partners' private details with other firms

questions.stem: Which action does most to build a public body's credibility with a community group?
options: Promising more than it can deliver to win support
Inviting the group to events only for photographs
Sending a different officer to every meeting
Doing what it said it would do, on time

questions.stem: Which approach gives a community the most real say in a partnership project?
options: Telling residents about the plan after it is final
Involving residents in setting priorities and decisions
Putting up a notice that invites written comments in a month
Asking residents to vote on the project's logo only

questions.stem: An agency wants to involve many small businesses in Ocho Rios at once. Which route is usually most efficient?
options: Visit every shop one by one on a single day
Advertise on one radio station for a month
Work through the local business association
Write to each owner at home using the tax roll

questions.stem: An agency put J$5 million into a community programme, and its business and community partners added J$15 million in cash and kind. How much did partners add for every J$1 of the agency's money?
A business partner and a community group disagree publicly over where a new playfield should go. What should the agency's partnership manager do first?
options: Bring them together to understand each side's interests
Side with the business, since it provides more of the money
Side with the community, since it has more members
Cancel the playfield so that no one is upset

questions.stem: Elderly residents in a hillside community in St Andrew rarely use the internet. How should an agency keep them informed about a partnership project?
options: Post updates only on the agency's social media page
Email monthly reports to every household
Publish updates on the agency's website only
Use community meetings, churches, flyers and radio

questions.stem: Why should a public body publicly thank and credit its community and business partners?
options: So partners will stop asking for anything in return
So the agency can take credit for their work later
It shows respect and encourages continued support
It is required before any partner can be paid

questions.stem: How can an agency best find out how its partners feel about working with it?
options: Assume all is well if no partner has complained
Ask partners regularly through a short survey or review
Ask only the agency's own staff what they think of partners
Count how many partners came to the last launch event

questions.stem: In a review, 36 of an agency's 48 partners rated the relationship as good or very good. What percentage is this?
An agency officer wants a municipal corporation's help with a market project. Through which route should the request normally go?
options: A private message to a councillor she knows
The council's proper official channels
A post on social media tagging the council
A complaint to the media about slow councils

questions.stem: Which feature most helps a community partnership to survive after the agency's funding ends?
options: Local people and groups have the skills to lead it
The agency's name and logo is on every sign and poster
One agency officer makes every decision for it
Funding is spent as fast as possible at the start

questions.stem: An agency officer from Kingston is building links with a Maroon community in Portland. What should she do?
options: Treat it exactly the same as any town in the Corporate Area
Expect the community to follow Kingston's customs
Arrange meetings at times that suit the agency only
Learn about and respect its leadership and traditions

questions.stem: Partners from a ministry, a bank and a youth club are planning a financial literacy programme. What should they agree first?
options: Who will appear in the newspaper photographs
Which partner's logo will be the largest on posters
How to divide any money left over at the end
The shared goal and what each partner will do

questions.stem: A partnership's home-visiting programme reached 2,400 of the 8,000 households in its target area. What percentage was reached?
How should a public body report back to a community on what a partnership has achieved?
options: Only in the agency's annual report to Parliament
In plain language, through local meetings and media
Through a technical report sent to the business partners
By waiting until the community asks for information

questions.stem: At the end of a successful year, a business partner sends an agency's partnership officer an expensive hamper. What should she do?
options: Keep it, since the partnership was a success
Share it with friends outside the office
Follow the gifts policy and declare it
Send it back with a complaint to the firm

questions.stem: Why should a manager in a public body attend parish development committee meetings and business forums, even when there is no current project?
options: To be seen at the events and enjoy the free refreshments
To build contacts and understand local priorities
To lobby for the manager's own political views
To collect business cards for personal use later

questions.stem: A community feeding programme depends on one supermarket for all its food. What risk should the agency manage?
options: The supermarket may sell too much of its food to other buyers
The programme may grow faster than planned
The programme may stop if the supermarket withdraws
Residents may prefer food from another shop

questions.stem: Partners in a community health programme want to share a list of residents' names and medical needs. What must happen first?
options: Each partner copies the list for its own records
The list is posted on the board at the community centre
The business partner uses it for marketing
Sharing is checked against the data protection law

questions.stem: Several partners are working to reduce school drop-out in a parish. Why should they agree a small set of shared measures?
options: So everyone can see joint progress toward the same goal
So each partner can avoid reporting its own results
So the partners need not meet with each other again
So the business partners can rank the schools publicly

questions.stem: A community leader says on local radio that an agency 'only comes around at election time'. What is the best response?
options: Meet the leader, listen and agree regular contact
Ask the radio station to stop the leader speaking
Issue a statement attacking the leader's motives
Ignore it, since radio comments do not matter

questions.stem: A business partner keeps failing to deliver what it promised, despite reminders. What should the partnership manager do?
options: Keep quiet so the relationship is not damaged
Discuss it openly and agree steps, then review the role
Announce in the media that the business is unreliable
Take over the business's tasks without telling anyone

questions.stem: A municipal corporation wants Jamaicans living overseas who were born in the parish to support its schools. Which approach is most suitable?
options: Wait for them to visit the parish when they are on holiday
Ask local schools to phone each person abroad
Send letters to every home asking for addresses
Work through diaspora associations and online meetings

questions.stem: A business partner asks an agency to use the partnership to lobby the government for a tax break for the business. What should the agency do?
options: Agree, since partners should support each other
Lobby quietly on the business's behalf so no one finds out
Decline, as it is outside the partnership's purpose
Pass the request on to the media for comment

questions.stem: Which is NOT a good way to maintain a long-term partnership with a community group?
options: Meeting regularly at times that suit the group
Sharing progress reports in plain language
Changing plans without telling the group
Recognising the group's contribution publicly

questions.stem: What should an agency's partnership engagement plan for the year set out?
options: The personal phone numbers of every partner's family
Only the events where the minister will be present
The partners' business secrets and pricing
Priority partners, aims, contact methods and timing

questions.stem: A partnership reports that it held 40 workshops. What else should it report to show its value to the community?
options: The number of chairs bought for the workshops
Changes in participants' jobs, skills or incomes
The number of photographs taken at each workshop
The brand of laptop used to make the slides

questions.stem: Why should an agency link its community partnership to the parish's local sustainable development plan?
options: It fits local priorities and joins up efforts
It allows the agency to ignore residents' views
It means no other agency can work in the parish
It removes the need to report on results

questions.stem: Attendance at a quarterly community and business forum fell from 120 to 90. What is the percentage fall?
What is the role of a 'partnership champion' inside a business that works with a public body?
options: To approve every payment the agency makes
To argue against the partnership inside the firm
To promote it inside the firm and keep it moving
To replace the agency's own partnership officer

questions.stem: An agency wants businesses, churches and the police to work together on safety in a Kingston community. Which first event is most suitable?
options: A facilitated meeting to agree shared concerns and ideas
A press conference announcing a finished plan
A dinner for business owners only
A letter instructing each group what to do

questions.stem: Several businesses want to sponsor a public agency's community programme. How should the agency choose among them?
options: Pick the business whose owner the director knows
Use clear, fair criteria and check for conflicts
Accept the first offer that arrives by email
Choose the one that promises the most publicity

questions.stem: After three years, a partnership with a business association is producing little. How should the agency decide its future?
options: Review results and views together, then agree next steps
End it by letter without speaking to the association
Continue it unchanged, since it has run for three years
Hand it over to another agency without telling the association

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What three-letter abbreviation is often used for a community-based organisation, such as a youth club or a citizens' association?
When businesses support communities, what does the abbreviation CSR stand for?
What two-word term describes the networks, trust and shared norms in a community that help people to work together?
An agency's J$8 million attracted J$20 million from its partners. How many J$ did partners add for every J$1 from the agency?
What two-word term describes organisations from different sectors agreeing a common agenda and shared measures to solve a complex social problem together?
What three-letter abbreviation names a non-profit organisation that is independent of government, such as a charity?
In Jamaica, what is the name of the parish-level body, often shortened to PDC, that brings community, government and business together to plan local development?
In a survey of 60 business partners, 48 said they would recommend partnering with the agency. What percentage is this?
What one word describes the standing a public body earns with partners by being reliable, honest and competent over time?
What two-word term names an open meeting held in a community so that residents can hear about and discuss a public project?
Attendance at partner meetings rose from 25 to 40. What is the percentage increase?
What three-letter abbreviation names the Jamaican public body that plans and supports social development in communities across the island?
What one word describes a partnership's ability to keep going and delivering benefits after its first funding ends?
A partnership reached 1,800 young people in its first year and 2,700 in its second year. What is the percentage increase?
What one word describes the good reputation and trust a business gains when it is seen to help the community?

essays.stem: Your agency wants to reduce crime among young men in an inner-city community in Kingston by working with community groups, other government bodies and local businesses. Plan how you would establish these partnerships.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start by learning about the community: reading the data on crime, unemployment and schooling, and walking the area with the local police and the parish's social development officers. I would map the community's assets and the possible partners in each sector: the citizens' association, churches, youth clubs and sports clubs; the police, the municipal corporation, schools and training agencies; and local shops, a bank branch and larger firms nearby. I would meet recognised community leaders first and listen to their views on the causes and what has worked, so the community is involved from the start rather than told what will happen. I would then approach each partner with a clear idea of what they could gain and give, for example apprenticeships from businesses or sports space from a church. A first joint meeting, facilitated fairly, would agree shared concerns, a goal and a few early actions. I would set up a simple partner register and an engagement plan, agree how decisions will be made and reported, and make sure the work stays politically neutral and respects confidentiality.
markingPoints: Researches the community and maps assets and partners in all three sectors
Meets community leaders first and listens
Approaches partners with a clear view of what each gains and gives
Holds a facilitated joint meeting to agree aims and early actions
Sets up a register, engagement plan and decision arrangements, staying neutral

essays.stem: Compare what usually motivates community, government and business partners, and explain how a public manager can bring these interests together around a shared goal.
essays.modelAnswer: Community partners, such as citizens' associations, churches and youth clubs, are usually motivated by improving life in their area: safety, jobs, services and respect. They bring local knowledge, trust and volunteers, but often have little money and limited time, and they want to be heard rather than told. Government partners are driven by their mandates, policy targets and accountability for public money. They bring funding, authority and services, but work through formal procedures that can be slow. Business partners want a healthy market, skilled workers, a good reputation and a safe place to operate, and some have a corporate social responsibility budget. They bring money, skills and speed, but need results they can show to owners and customers. A manager can bring these together by finding the overlap: for example, a skills programme gives youths jobs, helps a ministry meet its targets and gives firms trained staff. The manager should name the shared goal clearly, show each partner what it gains, respect each one's pace and limits, agree shared measures and recognise every partner's contribution publicly.
markingPoints: Explains the motivations and contributions of community partners
Explains the motivations and contributions of government partners
Explains the motivations and contributions of business partners
Identifies the overlap and frames a shared goal with an example
Describes practical ways to keep the interests aligned

essays.stem: A youth skills partnership in St James was funded by an agency (J$12 million), businesses (J$18 million in cash and J$6 million in kind) and community volunteers (time valued at J$4 million). It trained 3,200 young people. Calculate the agency's share of the total, how much partners added for each J$1 of agency money, and the total and agency cost per young person. Evaluate what these figures show.
essays.modelAnswer: The total resources were J$12 million + J$18 million + J$6 million + J$4 million = J$40 million. The agency's share was J$12 million ÷ J$40 million = 30%. Partners added J$28 million, so for every J$1 of agency money they added J$28 million ÷ J$12 million = about J$2.33. The total cost per young person was J$40 million ÷ 3,200 = J$12,500, and the cost to the agency was J$12 million ÷ 3,200 = J$3,750. These figures suggest the partnership gave good value for public money, since the agency reached many more young people than it could have alone. However, cost and numbers trained are only part of the picture. The agency should also check outcomes, such as how many found jobs or started businesses, and whether the in-kind and volunteer values were estimated fairly. It should also consider whether the business funding is likely to continue. If outcomes are strong, the figures give a good case to sustain the partnership and to recognise the business and community partners publicly.
markingPoints: Calculates the J$40 million total and the 30% agency share
Calculates about J$2.33 added per J$1 of agency money
Calculates J$12,500 total and J$3,750 agency cost per young person
Explains that outcomes, not only numbers trained, must be checked
Notes the reliability of in-kind values or the risk to future funding, and draws a conclusion

essays.stem: Describe the practices a public body should use to maintain strong relationships with its community, government and business partners over several years.
essays.modelAnswer: A public body should keep a partner register that records each partner's contacts, interests, commitments and history, so that relationships do not depend on one officer's memory. It should have an engagement plan that sets out how often and how it will contact each priority partner, such as quarterly meetings with the municipal corporation, monthly updates to community groups and an annual forum with business. It should keep its promises and explain early when something cannot be delivered, because reliability builds trust. Communication should suit each partner: plain-language updates and community meetings for residents, formal letters and official channels for government bodies, and short, results-focused reports for businesses. Partners should be asked for their views regularly through reviews or short surveys, and the body should show how it acted on them. Achievements should be shared and each partner credited publicly. When officers change jobs, there should be a proper handover and introductions. Finally, the body should behave ethically and neutrally, declaring gifts and conflicts, so partners trust that it treats everyone fairly.
markingPoints: Keeps a partner register and an engagement plan
Keeps promises and communicates early about problems
Tailors communication to each type of partner
Seeks feedback, acts on it and recognises partners
Manages handovers and behaves ethically and neutrally

essays.stem: Explain the ethical risks a public body faces when it works in partnership with politicians, businesses and community groups, and how a manager should manage them.
essays.modelAnswer: One risk is political: elected representatives may wish to use a partnership to gain support, for example by launching it at a party event or deciding which communities benefit. A public body must stay neutral, so the manager should use official events, apply fair criteria for where services go and treat representatives of all parties equally. A second risk is that business partners may expect favours, such as contracts, faster licences or lobbying in return for sponsorship. The manager should keep partnership activities separate from regulatory and procurement decisions, choose sponsors by clear criteria and write down what each side gives and receives. A third risk is conflicts of interest and gifts, where officers have personal links to partners or receive valuable items; these must be declared under the code of conduct and gifts policy. A fourth risk is misuse of personal information shared between partners, which must follow the data protection law in general terms. Finally, community groups can be used as a front for private interests. Openness, written agreements, declarations and regular review help keep partnerships ethical and trusted.
markingPoints: Identifies political risks and how to stay neutral
Identifies business expectations of favour and how to keep decisions separate
Covers conflicts of interest and gifts, with declaration
Covers data protection in general terms
Explains openness, records and review as safeguards

essays.stem: In a coastal partnership, a large hotel group and a ministry dominate decisions, while small fishers and vendors feel ignored. Evaluate how the partnership manager could make the partnership more inclusive.
essays.modelAnswer: Power imbalances are common when large organisations sit with small groups, and they matter because the people most affected may be the least heard, which weakens trust and results. The manager could change how meetings work: hold some on the beach or in the fishing village at times when fishers are not at sea, use plain language rather than technical terms, and have a neutral facilitator who invites quieter members to speak. Smaller listening sessions with fishers and vendors before big meetings would let them prepare and speak through chosen representatives. The manager could also give these groups real roles, such as a seat on the steering group and a say in setting priorities, not just a chance to comment. Support such as travel costs or training in meeting skills may help. These steps take time and may slow decisions, and the hotel group may resist sharing control, so the manager must explain the benefits: better local knowledge, fewer conflicts and a stronger reputation. Checking regularly whether all groups feel heard shows whether the changes work.
markingPoints: Explains why power imbalances matter
Suggests changes to meeting time, place, language and facilitation
Gives smaller groups real roles in decisions and practical support
Evaluates drawbacks, such as time and resistance, and how to handle them
Checks regularly whether all groups feel heard

essays.stem: A business partner and a community group in a town partnership disagree strongly about late-night noise from a new entertainment venue. As the public body's partnership manager, explain how you would handle the conflict.
essays.modelAnswer: I would act early, before positions harden or the dispute spreads further in the media. I would first meet each side separately to listen and understand their interests: the business wants enough trading hours to be profitable, while residents want sleep and safety for their children. I would gather facts, such as noise readings, the venue's licence conditions and the times of complaints, and check which other agencies, such as the police or the municipal corporation, have a role. Then I would bring the two sides together in a facilitated meeting with ground rules, focusing on interests rather than positions and looking for options, such as sound limits, speakers facing away from homes, earlier closing on weeknights and a phone number for complaints. Any agreement would be written down with who does what, and reviewed after a month. I would stay neutral, keep both sides informed and avoid taking public sides. If agreement cannot be reached, I would refer the matter to the body with authority to decide, while keeping both relationships respectful for future work.
markingPoints: Acts early and listens to each side separately
Gathers facts and identifies agencies with a role
Runs a facilitated meeting focused on interests and options
Records the agreement with actions and a review date
Stays neutral and refers to the proper authority if needed

essays.stem: Recommend how a public body should review the value and health of its network of community, government and business partnerships each year, and how it should use the results.
essays.modelAnswer: I would recommend a yearly review with two parts: results and relationships. For results, the body should compare each partnership's outcomes with its shared measures, such as jobs gained, households reached or improvements in services, and look at the resources partners added for each J$1 of public money. For relationships, it should run a short survey or interviews asking partners whether communication is good, commitments are kept, decisions are fair and they would recommend working with the body. Staff who manage the partnerships should add their views, and attendance and activity records can show whether partners are still engaged. The results should be summarised in a short report that rates each partnership, for example as strong, needing attention or ending. The body should then act: strengthen what works, agree improvement steps with partners where relationships are weak, and close or change partnerships that no longer serve their purpose, after discussing it openly with the partners. The findings should be shared with partners and the community, and used to update the engagement plan for the next year.
markingPoints: Reviews results against shared measures and resources added
Reviews relationship quality through partner feedback
Uses staff views and engagement records
Rates partnerships and decides to strengthen, improve or close them openly
Shares findings and updates the engagement plan

essays.stem: Plan a communication approach for a partnership between a municipal corporation, three government agencies, a farmers' group and two agro-processing firms that is improving farm roads and markets in St Elizabeth.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start by listing the audiences and what each needs. Farmers need practical news about road works, market days and how to take part, in plain language. The government agencies need progress against targets and issues for decision, through formal channels. The firms need short updates on supply, quality and dates. Councillors and the wider public need to know what is happening and who is involved. For farmers, I would use meetings at the farmers' group, notices at shops and churches, local radio and a WhatsApp group run by the group's secretary, so that those without internet are still reached. For agencies and the council, I would send a monthly one-page progress report and hold a quarterly partners' meeting with minutes. For the firms, a short email update and visits would suit. I would agree one set of key messages so all partners say the same thing, and agree who may speak to the media. Every partner would be credited fairly. Finally, I would ask partners and farmers whether the information is reaching them and adjust the approach if it is not.
markingPoints: Identifies the audiences and what each needs
Chooses suitable channels, including ones for people without internet
Sets regular formal reporting for government partners
Agrees key messages, media spokespeople and fair credit
Checks whether communication works and adjusts

essays.stem: A partnership led by a government agency has improved services in a rural community, but the agency's funding will end in eighteen months. Explain how the agency should prepare so that the partnership and its benefits continue.
essays.modelAnswer: The agency should plan for the change now, not in the last months. First, it should agree with partners which activities matter most to keep, based on the results so far. It should build local leadership by training community members and groups in planning, finance, record keeping and running meetings, and gradually hand them more of the decisions. It should look for other sources of support: business partners may continue sponsorship if they see results, other government bodies may take over parts that fit their mandates, and the community may raise some funds or provide volunteers. Links to the parish development committee and the local development plan can help the work stay on others' agendas. The agency should make sure records, contacts and simple procedures are handed over so knowledge is not lost. A written transition plan should set out who will do what, with dates, and be agreed with all partners. The agency should tell the community openly what will change. After it steps back, it can still keep in light contact and review how the partnership is doing.
markingPoints: Starts planning early and agrees what to keep with partners
Builds local leadership and skills, handing over decisions gradually
Finds other sources of support across sectors
Hands over records and agrees a written transition plan
Communicates openly and keeps light contact afterwards

practical1.title: Map partners and plan engagement for a community issue
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a made-up case: a public body (for example a parish municipal corporation or a government agency) wants to tackle a community issue, such as youth unemployment or a run-down market district, by working with community groups, other government bodies and local businesses. The pack describes the community, its groups, the agencies active there and local businesses. As a group, prepare a partner map and an engagement plan. Each member has a named role: community lead (identifies community partners and assets, and what each wants and can give); government liaison lead (identifies the government bodies involved, their mandates and the proper channels to approach them); business liaison lead (identifies business partners, their interests and what would persuade them, and checks for conflicts of interest); engagement planner (combines the work into a power and interest map and a one-year engagement plan with aims, contact methods, frequency and owners); and correspondence officer (drafts one approach letter to a business and one invitation to a community meeting, both politically neutral). In a group of four, the engagement planner also drafts the letters. Every member presents their part of the map and plan to the assessor.
materials: Flipchart paper, sticky notes and markers for the map
Computers with word processing and spreadsheet software
Partner register and engagement plan templates
photos: The partner map on flipchart, showing all three sectors
The approach letter and the meeting invitation
The group presenting to the assessor
checklist: Took a named role and completed their part of the evidence
Partners from all three sectors are identified with their interests and contributions
Government bodies are approached through proper channels
Conflicts of interest and political neutrality are addressed
The engagement plan sets clear aims, methods, frequency and owners
Letters are clear, respectful and politically neutral
Presented their part clearly and answered the assessor's questions
safety: Use only the made-up case; do not use real people's or firms' details
Keep the case pack confidential and return it to the assessor
Respect each other's ideas and share the workload fairly
Take a short screen break each hour

practical2.title: Facilitate a cross-sector partners' forum and follow it up
practical2.brief: Using a made-up case from the assessor (for example a partnership to improve a town centre, with a progress update and a disagreement between partners), your group holds a 40-minute partners' forum and then produces the follow-up. Each member has a named role: facilitator from the public body (prepares the agenda and ground rules, runs the forum fairly and keeps it to time); community representative (raises residents' concerns from a role card); business representative (raises business concerns from a role card); government agency representative (explains what the agency can and cannot do within its mandate); and recorder (writes the notes of views, agreements and actions). In a group of four, the facilitator also covers the government agency's role card. The forum must review progress, work through the disagreement by looking at interests, and agree at least four joint actions with owners and dates. After the forum, the group writes the forum notes, a one-page thank-you and update letter to all partners that credits each one fairly, and a short partner feedback survey of six to eight questions to review the relationship. Every member writes or checks part of these documents.
materials: Case pack, progress update and role cards from the assessor
Agenda, notes, letter and survey templates
Computer and printer, or paper and pens
photos: The forum in progress (faces only if all agree)
The flipchart of interests and options for the disagreement
The forum notes with agreed actions
The thank-you and update letter and the partner feedback survey
checklist: Took a named role and prepared for it
The facilitator ran the forum fairly, kept time and drew out every voice
The disagreement was handled by exploring interests and options, not by taking sides
Agreed actions have owners and dates and are recorded accurately
The letter credits each partner fairly and is politically neutral
The feedback survey asks clear questions about communication, trust and results
safety: Keep role cards and notes confidential; return them to the assessor
